title: Joe Steele, pianist who guarded his hands
summary: Joe Steele, whose sister taught Holmes in Sunday School, played classical and dance piano, protected his fingers carefully, yet loved baseball.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I thought we could flesh out a few of the musicians who you used to know -- or still know. For instance, Joe Steele.
Joe Steele. Great man of the piano. One

of his sisters was my Sunday School teacher when I was a little boy. And Joe was a great pianist, at that time playing Classical Music and dance music, as it was called in those days -- just the beginning of Jazz. The name "Jazz" wasn't used in all families. So he was a great dance pianist.
Do you know where he came from?
I'm sure he was some part of Georgia. I think it was Atlanta. But on that I'm not too sure.
Because apparently he was a graduate of the New England Conservatory.
Now, you said about some of his idiosyncracies...

Well, he had little weird ideas. Well, not weird, but a little strange. He was so wrapped up with his music and his hands and his fingers, he wouldn't shake hands with a stranger or anything like that because he was always protecting his fingers. And sometimes he would have his hands folded, like the Chinese used to hold their hands years ago, keep them close to his side and covered over, just to keep his fingers from getting hurt. And next time you'd see him, he'd be in the street there playing hard ball. He was a great pianist, but he loved baseball, too, and he loved to play.
So he didn't worry about his hands then, but...
But anything else, he worried about his fingers.
...anything else he worried about his fingers.
